question: What does a single adult or a small household realistically spend each month on rent or a mortgage, food, utilities, transportation, insurance and other necessities, and how does that change between a small town and a city, and across states? What does a shop assistant or stock clerk's pay leave after that?

title: What an ordinary person spends to live each month, by place
usableAnswer: Monthly spending bands by category for a single adult and for a small household, with how they vary by place size and by state or region, and a named public source for each so the game can refresh it. Say which items are fixed monthly bills and which vary with how a person lives.
whyItMatters: Nobody in the game pays for anything. Fatima worked a part-time shop job in Eastport, Maine for three years and saved $87,984 because rent, food and bills do not exist. Money never forces a choice, so a job, a raise or a campaign donation means nothing.

findings.estimate: CE2024 one-person all-category annual mean $48,794 = $4,066.17/month; extracted SE $928.11/year. This is a consumer-unit mean including insurance/pensions, not a subsistence minimum. All-consumer-unit regional means span $70,376–$92,625/year; these cannot be applied as per-person costs.
findings.spread: Use the extracted household-size/category SE-based sampling intervals and region/size differences. No invented town-size or territory premium.
findings.mechanism: Bills follow actual household size, tenure, commuting, care/health needs and prices; use ACS/HUD actual place housing data where available.
findings.gaps: No all56 place-level joint size/region/local-vendor consumption survey. Territories are proxy-only. National $4,066/month is not an exact state figure.
